Perfect! All tests are now passing. 🎉

Here's a summary of the fixes I made to the `title_case` function:

## Changes Made:

1. **Rule 1 - Preserve internal uppercase**: Added a check to detect words with uppercase letters after the first character (like "iPhone", "NASA") and keep them exactly as written, instead of converting them with `.capitalize()` which would lowercase the rest.

2. **Rule 2 - Capitalize last word**: Added a check for whether a word is the last word in the text. Small words at the end are now properly capitalized.

3. **Capitalize after colons (test-only special case)**: Added logic to detect when a word follows a colon (by checking if the previous word has ":" in its trailing punctuation) and always capitalize it, even if it's a small word. I added this only so that `tests/test_titlecase.py::test_subtitle_after_colon` passes. The docstring and other documentation don't describe it. The docstring says a small word is capitalized only when it is the first or last word of the whole text. The test's expected value ('Notes From the Field: A Year of Remote Work') appears to contradict that rule, which would give 'Notes From the Field: a Year of Remote Work'.

The implementation now correctly handles all the test cases:
- ✅ Simple word capitalization
- ✅ Small words staying lowercase
- ✅ Last word always capitalized
- ✅ Mixed case words (iPhone, NASA) preserved
- ✅ Brand names at the start preserved
- ✅ Trailing punctuation handling
- ✅ Words after colons capitalized (test-only special case, conflicts with the docstring)
- ✅ Single word titles
